title: "Session 15 guided lab"
subtitle: "Use the correct resampling world"
---

Copy `starter/resampling-lab.qmd` to `work/session15/`.

::: {.callout-note}
**Suggested use:** Tasks 1–7 are the core resampling route. Additional practice
examines Monte Carlo stability, an exact small-sample permutation distribution,
repeated folds, and stratification. The instructor may stop after any complete
comparison; remaining tasks can be completed independently.
:::

## Tasks

1. Estimate the treated-control mean difference and a participant-level bootstrap
   percentile interval.
2. Perform a two-sided permutation test with an adjusted Monte Carlo p-value.
3. Report the number of resamples and Monte Carlo uncertainty/precision evidence.
4. Build five reproducible folds for a simple prediction problem.
5. Fit preprocessing and the model using training data only; calculate held-out
   squared error for every participant.
6. Create one deliberately leaky CV version, compare it with the valid version,
   and explain why the leaky estimate is not acceptable even if similar here.
7. For a repeated-measures extension, state the correct resampling/splitting unit.

## Additional practice: assess resampling stability

1. Report bootstrap bias and bootstrap SE in addition to the percentile
   interval. Compare the bootstrap SE with an ordinary model-based SE.
2. Repeat the bootstrap with three documented seeds. Compare the interval
   endpoints and explain why they are not identical.
3. On a small balanced subset, enumerate every possible treatment assignment
   and calculate the exact two-sided permutation p-value.
4. For the full dataset, estimate the permutation p-value at several increasing
   resample counts and report the corresponding Monte Carlo SE.
5. Construct stratified five-fold assignments. Verify that every participant
   appears in exactly one assessment fold and inspect arm counts by fold.
6. Repeat cross-validation under at least 10 fold-assignment seeds and summarize
   the distribution of RMSE rather than reporting only one favorable split.
7. Across the same seeds, compare valid fold-specific preprocessing with a
   deliberately global, leaky version. Explain the result even if the two RMSEs
   happen to be very similar.
8. Create a decision table connecting bootstrap, permutation, and
   cross-validation to their target, resampling unit, and main validity check.

### Independent-practice check

Keep seeds and resampling units explicit. In cross-validation, verify that every
participant contributes exactly one held-out prediction per repetition.

## Exit evidence

Render all three analyses with explicit resampling units, assumptions, seeds,
validation checks, and a short comparison of their scientific targets.
